reviews.title: Too many matches with confused people
reviews.text:
I've been using Coffee Meets Bagel (CMB) on and off for almost 8 years, and I've also subscribed to the premium service. Over the years, I've matched with a lot of women, so I feel I have enough experience to leave an honest review.

The biggest issue with this app is the quality of the dating pool. From my experience, many of the profiles I match with fall into one of these categories: fake accounts, people who seem more interested in financial support than a genuine relationship, recently divorced individuals, people who have just come out of a relationship and are only exploring, single parents, or profiles that don't accurately represent the person. Even with selfie verification now available, these issues still exist.

Of course, there are genuine people on the app, but they seem to be a small minority. I've also found that many matches aren't clear about what they're looking for, which often leads to conversations that go nowhere and a lot of wasted time for people who are genuinely looking for a relationship.

I hope CMB invests more effort into improving the quality of its user base by removing fake profiles, encouraging users to clearly state their dating intentions, and creating a better matching experience. People join dating apps to find meaningful connections—not to keep paying for subscriptions while spending most of their time filtering through inactive, misleading, or incompatible profiles.

I expect your urgent attention and a formal written response, not a generic template reply.

Yours faithfully,

Eddy

reviews.title: Unreliable Messaging & Dismissive Support
reviews.text:
I had a really disappointing experience with this app that affected a real life date.

There was an issue with message delivery on the app. My match and I had agreed to meet, but due to a missing or undelivered message, the plan didn’t get properly confirmed. I showed up, only to realise the date wasn’t happening. This isn’t just an “app glitch” it wastes people’s time and effort, especially when safety and trust already matter so much in online dating.

What’s more frustrating is the response from support. Instead of properly investigating or acknowledging the possibility of a system issue, they simply stated that “all messages were delivered successfully” and dismissed the concern. No transparency, no attempt to actually verify the conversation from a user perspective.

Dating apps rely heavily on reliable communication. If users can’t trust that messages are being delivered correctly, the whole experience breaks down.
